newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Egypt says it can do no more for Boutros-Ghali.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says it can do no more for Boutros-Ghali.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said on Tuesday Egypt could do no more to help Boutros Boutros-Ghali win a second term as U.N. secretary general after the United States vetoed his reappointment.

"Our mission had reached its limits after 14 countries voted for him and one was against him," Mubarak said when asked whether Egypt still supported the longtime Egyptian diplomat. "The issue is now over and if Boutros-Ghali wants to maintain his candidacy it is up to him."

The 15-member Security Council voted last month by 14 to one to reappoint Boutros-Ghali, but the United States, one of five veto-wielding permanent members, voted against him because it blames him for doing too little to reform the cash-strapped body.

At the United Nations, Mubarak's comments raised concern as to whether Egypt was dropping its campaign to re-elect Boutros-Ghali. But U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa said he had spoken to Mubarak on Tuesday and the Egyptian president said his comments "were taken out of context and that Egypt would continue to support his re-election."
Mubarak was speaking at a news conference just before leaving Tunis after a meeting with Tunisian President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali.
